en.greeting: Hi! You can talk about the past now, so today we'll tell stories: what happened first, what happened next, and what happened because of it. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Order words for stories
steps.text: In A1 you told your normal day with **first, then, after that, finally**. Now use them for a story in the **past**.
steps.body: **First** = the first event. **Then**, **next** and **after that** = the events in the middle: they mean almost the same, so mix them. **Finally** = the last event, or the end of a long wait (= akhirnya). The verbs are in the past simple: *went, had, bought*. Commas: usually after *First, Next, After that, Finally*; usually not after *Then*. Careful: **After** alone isn't **after that**: say *After that, we …*, not 'After, we …'.

steps.title: Dewi's trip to Yogyakarta
steps.text: Here's a short story. Look at the order words and the past verbs.
steps.body: **Then, Next** and **After that** are all in the middle: you could swap them. **First** and **Finally** can't move.

examples.en: Last weekend, Dewi went to Yogyakarta.
examples.id: Akhir pekan lalu, Dewi pergi ke Yogyakarta.

examples.en: Then she had gudeg for lunch.
examples.id: Lalu dia makan gudeg untuk makan siang.

examples.en: After that, she bought some batik.
Finally, she took the train home.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina tells you about her Saturday.

question.prompt: Rina: '___, I cleaned my room. Then I went to the market. After that, I cooked lunch.'
question.explanation: Cleaning the room is the **first** event, so start with **First**. Finally is for the last event, and After alone needs something after it (*after that, after lunch*).

steps.title: before, after, when
steps.text: Now join two events in **one** sentence.
steps.body: **before** (sebelum), **after** (setelah) and **when** (ketika, saat: at that moment) + a **subject + verb** (the subject = who does it): *after **I finished** work*. Or a noun: *after work*. This part can go first (with a comma) or second (no comma). Indonesian trap: *Setelah selesai kerja, **lalu** saya pulang*. In English, after already shows the order, so **no then**: *After I finished work, I went home.* And both verbs stay in the past.

pairs.en: When I got to the station, …

steps.title: Same order, three ways
steps.text: **before** and **after** don't change what happened first. Look at the order of the events, not the order of the words.

timeline.title: Rina's evening
timeline.caption: After Rina finished work, she went home. = Rina went home after she finished work. = Before Rina went home, she finished work. In all three, she finished work first.

steps.title: Which came first?
steps.text: Look at the times, then choose.

question.prompt: The film started at 7:00. We got to the cinema at 7:15. Complete: The film started ___ we got to the cinema.
question.explanation: 7:00 comes before 7:15: the film started first, so use **before**. after would mean we were there first, and when would mean the same moment.

steps.title: Spot the right sentence
steps.text: Only one of these is correct English.

options: After the meeting ended, then we had lunch.
After the meeting ended, we had lunch.
After the meeting end, we had lunch.
question.explanation: **after** already shows the order, so there's no *then* in the second part (Indonesian *lalu*). In a story both verbs are in the past: *ended*, not *end*.

steps.title: so for the result
steps.text: You know **because** for a reason. Its partner is **so**, for a result.
steps.body: **reason, so result**: *I was tired, so I went to bed early.* = *I went to bed early **because** I was tired.* One sentence takes **so** or **because**, never both: Indonesian *Karena …, jadi …* becomes 'Because …, so …', which is wrong. Second trap: **akhirnya** often means *jadi* (*Hujan, akhirnya saya di rumah*): that's **so**, not finally.

pairs.en: I was tired, so I went to bed early.
pairs.id: Saya capek, jadi saya tidur lebih awal.

pairs.en: I went to bed early because I was tired.
pairs.id: Saya tidur lebih awal karena saya capek.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Think about the Indonesian: *Hujan deras, akhirnya kami tidak jadi ke pantai.*

question.prompt: It rained a lot, ___ we didn't go to the beach.
question.explanation: The rain is the reason and not going is the result, so use **so**. *finally* is the *akhirnya* trap: it's only for the last event. *because* would make 'we didn't go' the reason for the rain.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Reason first, then **so** and the result.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Sari lapar, jadi dia membeli martabak.
question.solution: Sari was hungry, so she bought a martabak.
question.explanation: The reason (*Sari was hungry*) comes first, then a comma, **so**, and the result (*she bought a martabak*).

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for when you write your next story.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Linking words for stories
artifact.intro: Tell the story in the past simple. Order the events, join them, and show results.
rows: First, we took the bus to Bogor.
Then we had lunch. After that, we visited the park.
the last event, or the end of a long wait
I had a coffee before I went to work.
After I got home, I cooked dinner.
When I got to the station, the train was there.
The bus was late, so I took an ojek.
I took an ojek because the bus was late.
tips: **after / before** already show the order: no **then** in the second part. Comma only when the after/before/when part comes first.
**so** or **because**, never both: not 'Because the bus was late, so …'.
**akhirnya** = *jadi* → **so**; **akhirnya** after a long wait or the last event → **Finally**.

examples.en: When the rain stopped, we went out.
The shop was closed, so we went home.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? This video explains the order words, and this page has a short A2 story to read and write.

id.greeting: Hai! Sekarang kamu sudah bisa membicarakan masa lalu, jadi hari ini kita akan bercerita: apa yang terjadi pertama, apa yang terjadi berikutnya, dan apa akibatnya. Ayo kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Kata urutan untuk bercerita
steps.text: Di A1 kamu menceritakan hari biasamu dengan **first, then, after that, finally**. Sekarang pakai kata-kata itu untuk cerita di **masa lalu**.
steps.body: **First** = kejadian pertama. **Then**, **next** dan **after that** = kejadian di tengah: artinya hampir sama, jadi pakai bergantian. **Finally** = kejadian terakhir, atau akhir dari menunggu lama (= akhirnya). Kata kerjanya past simple: *went, had, bought*. Koma: biasanya setelah *First, Next, After that, Finally*; biasanya tidak setelah *Then*. Hati-hati: **After** saja bukan **after that**: katakan *After that, we …*, bukan 'After, we …'.

steps.title: Perjalanan Dewi ke Yogyakarta
steps.text: Ini cerita pendek. Perhatikan kata urutan dan kata kerja past-nya.
steps.body: **Then, Next** dan **After that** semuanya di tengah: boleh ditukar. **First** dan **Finally** tidak bisa dipindah.

examples.en: Last weekend, Dewi went to Yogyakarta.
examples.id: Akhir pekan lalu, Dewi pergi ke Yogyakarta.

examples.en: Then she had gudeg for lunch.
examples.id: Lalu dia makan gudeg untuk makan siang.

examples.en: After that, she bought some batik.
Finally, she took the train home.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina bercerita tentang hari Sabtunya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi cerita Rina: '___, I cleaned my room. Then I went to the market. After that, I cooked lunch.'
question.explanation: Membersihkan kamar adalah kejadian **pertama**, jadi mulai dengan **First**. Finally untuk kejadian terakhir, dan After saja butuh sesuatu di belakangnya (*after that, after lunch*).

steps.title: before, after, when
steps.text: Sekarang gabungkan dua kejadian dalam **satu** kalimat.
steps.body: **before** (sebelum), **after** (setelah) dan **when** (ketika, saat: pada saat itu) + **subjek + kata kerja** (subjek = siapa yang melakukan): *after **I finished** work*. Atau kata benda: *after work*. Bagian ini boleh di depan (pakai koma) atau di belakang (tanpa koma). Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Setelah selesai kerja, **lalu** saya pulang*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, after sudah menunjukkan urutan, jadi **tanpa then**: *After I finished work, I went home.* Dan kedua kata kerjanya tetap past.

pairs.en: When I got to the station, …

steps.title: Urutan sama, tiga cara
steps.text: **before** dan **after** tidak mengubah apa yang terjadi duluan. Lihat urutan kejadiannya, bukan urutan katanya.

timeline.title: Sore hari Rina
timeline.caption: After Rina finished work, she went home. = Rina went home after she finished work. = Before Rina went home, she finished work. Di ketiganya, Rina selesai kerja duluan.

steps.title: Mana yang duluan?
steps.text: Lihat jamnya, lalu pilih.

question.prompt: Filmnya mulai jam 7:00. Kami sampai di bioskop jam 7:15. Lengkapi: The film started ___ we got to the cinema.
question.explanation: 7:00 lebih dulu dari 7:15: filmnya mulai duluan, jadi pakai **before**. after berarti kami sampai duluan, dan when berarti pada saat yang sama.

steps.title: Cari kalimat yang benar
steps.text: Hanya satu yang benar dalam bahasa Inggris.

options: After the meeting ended, then we had lunch.
After the meeting ended, we had lunch.
After the meeting end, we had lunch.
question.explanation: **after** sudah menunjukkan urutan, jadi tidak ada *then* di bagian kedua (*lalu* dalam bahasa Indonesia). Dalam cerita, kedua kata kerjanya past: *ended*, bukan *end*.

steps.title: so untuk akibat
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal **because** untuk alasan. Pasangannya adalah **so**, untuk akibat.
steps.body: **alasan, so akibat**: *I was tired, so I went to bed early.* = *I went to bed early **because** I was tired.* Satu kalimat memakai **so** atau **because**, jangan dua-duanya: *Karena …, jadi …* jadi 'Because …, so …', dan itu salah. Jebakan kedua: **akhirnya** sering berarti *jadi* (*Hujan, akhirnya saya di rumah*): itu **so**, bukan finally.

pairs.en: I was tired, so I went to bed early.
pairs.id: Saya capek, jadi saya tidur lebih awal.

pairs.en: I went to bed early because I was tired.
pairs.id: Saya tidur lebih awal karena saya capek.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pikirkan kalimat Indonesianya: *Hujan deras, akhirnya kami tidak jadi ke pantai.*

question.prompt: Lengkapi: It rained a lot, ___ we didn't go to the beach.
question.explanation: Hujan adalah alasannya dan tidak jadi pergi adalah akibatnya, jadi pakai **so**. *finally* adalah jebakan *akhirnya*: kata itu hanya untuk kejadian terakhir. *because* akan membuat 'kami tidak pergi' menjadi alasan hujannya.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Alasan dulu, lalu **so** dan akibatnya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Sari lapar, jadi dia membeli martabak.
question.solution: Sari was hungry, so she bought a martabak.
question.explanation: Alasannya (*Sari was hungry*) di depan, lalu koma, **so**, dan akibatnya (*she bought a martabak*).

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk saat kamu menulis cerita berikutnya.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Kata penghubung untuk bercerita
artifact.intro: Ceritakan dengan past simple. Urutkan kejadiannya, gabungkan, dan tunjukkan akibatnya.
rows: First, we took the bus to Bogor.
Then we had lunch. After that, we visited the park.
kejadian terakhir, atau akhir dari menunggu lama
I had a coffee before I went to work.
After I got home, I cooked dinner.
When I got to the station, the train was there.
The bus was late, so I took an ojek.
I took an ojek because the bus was late.
tips: **after / before** sudah menunjukkan urutan: tidak ada **then** di bagian kedua. Koma hanya kalau bagian after/before/when ada di depan.
**so** atau **because**, jangan dua-duanya: bukan 'Because the bus was late, so …'.
**akhirnya** = *jadi* → **so**; **akhirnya** setelah menunggu lama atau kejadian terakhir → **Finally**.

examples.en: When the rain stopped, we went out.
The shop was closed, so we went home.

steps.title: Belajar lebih lanjut
steps.text: Mau latihan lagi? Video ini menjelaskan kata-kata urutan, dan halaman ini punya cerita pendek level A2 untuk dibaca dan latihan menulis.
